summary:
Build attempt 2 (160f400) changes only T-008 in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1: four new rows in its $bad table and a rewritten comment above the case. `git diff cd235ca 160f400` shows no other change to src, the hook or docs, and the working tree differs from HEAD only in .taad metadata.

I ran `WindowCases.ps1 -Case T-008` and it passed all 8 values (exit 0). Each new row ended with 0xE0434352, wrote no report, and left one refusal line that its anchored regex matched:
- '|2|995' → ArgumentException "'' is not one folder's name (Parameter 'folderName')".
- 'a\b|2|995' → the same refusal for 'a\b'.
- 'folder1|2|18' → ArgumentOutOfRangeException "… (Parameter 'win32Error') Actual value was 18."
- 'folder1|2|x' → FormatException "the error 'x' is not a whole number".

If any of those refusals regressed, the hook would arm and the size-mode launch would write a report and exit 0. The exit and no-report checks would then fail the case, so each row really tests its refusal.

What the tree now says about T-008 is still true:
- The new comment above T-008 lists every value the table feeds.
- WindowCases.ps1's header and docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md both say only that T-008 is 'a value the hook cannot arm, which ends the app before its Main'.
- The refusals the ArmFailListing comment lists in StartupHook.cs are ones the code makes.

Everything else that round 1 verified sits on code that has not changed since: the failpoint placement, T-007, the mutants, Core.Tests 414/414, fitness and rules-parity. I did not re-run `-Case All` this lap, because the only changed function, Test-T008, passed on its own.

Nothing was left open that blocks this review. The bug report was only a title. As in round 1, I took the Core scanner test to be already built (it was cut from the slice), so only the window case and the seam it needs were owed.

Second round: I found nothing new on this pass. The attempt only adds four rows and their regexes to T-008's bad-value table, and each row tests the refusal it names.

- **Where each refusal comes from:** the hook's parser (StartupHook.cs ArmFailListing) checks only the part count and that the page and error are whole numbers. It passes an empty name, 'a\b' and error 18 through to Core. So the rows for '|2|995', 'a\b|2|995' and 'folder1|2|18' each reach Core's own refusal in SynchronousIoCancel.FailListingOf.
- **If a refusal regressed:** the hook would arm, and the size-mode launch would write a report and exit 0. T-008's exit and no-report checks would then fail, so no row can pass while the refusal it names is broken.
- **The regexes match the log as written:** Log calls ReplaceLineEndings(" ") on each line, so ArgumentOutOfRangeException's two-line message becomes one line and the anchored 'Actual value was 18\.$' matches. The 'a\b' row escapes the backslash correctly in the regex, and the value is literal in the single-quoted PowerShell string.
- **Case-insensitive matching:** PowerShell's `-match` ignores case, which only makes the reason checks looser, not wrong.
- **One run per value:** each value gets its own launch and its own single-line check. The error-0 regex, which is not anchored at the end, therefore cannot be satisfied by another row's line.
- **The run:** I re-ran T-008 this lap and all eight values produced exactly those lines, 0xE0434352 and no report.

obligations.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-T008 $bad now also holds 'folder1|2|x', 'folder1|2|18', '|2|995' and 'a\b|2|995', each with a regex anchored to its own refusal. I re-ran T-008: all 8 launches were refused with exit -532462766, no report and one matching hook line, and the case PASSED.

src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/DirectoryReader.cs:109-124 is unchanged since cd235ca. The substitution still runs after io.Query and before the error check, and only on a call that returned 0. Query settles an issued cancel to Aborted (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:278-296), so earlier pages are kept.

T-008 now feeds every refusal the design contract and the code make: wrong part count, a non-numeric page and error, page 1, error 0, error 18, an empty name and a separator. The missing-member shape is still covered by the NoFailListingMember mutant (verified in round 1; unchanged).

cases.evidence: Test-T008 in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 launches eight malformed or refused values, each separately in the hook's size mode. It asserts 0xE0434352, no report and a single refusal line matching that value's own reason. I re-ran it and it passed. A Core member reflection cannot find is fed by the NoFailListingMember mutant.

drift: Nothing new departed in this attempt. The only change is T-008's bad-value table and its comment. Every departure declared in attempt 1 still stands as it was reviewed.
